description: Published MCP tool manifest. shared_tools and backend_only_tools are generated from the hosted server (backend/api/chatgpt/tool_manifest.py); cli_only_tools belongs to the CLI, which keeps a byte copy of this file and tests its own tools against it (scripts/utils/check_mcp_tool_manifest.py compares the two). A shared tool has one title, description, input schema and annotations in both servers.

shared_tools.name: promptguard_scan_text
shared_tools.title: Scan text for threats
shared_tools.description:
Scan text for security threats including prompt injection, jailbreaks, PII leakage, and toxic content. Returns a decision (allow/block), confidence score, threat type, and reason. Each call counts as one Request on your PromptGuard plan.
When to use: When reviewing user-facing prompts, testing LLM inputs for safety, or verifying that content is free of injection attacks before sending to an LLM.

text.description: The text content to scan for security threats

content_type.description: Whether the text is a prompt sent to a model or a model's response

shared_tools.name: promptguard_redact
shared_tools.title: Redact PII
shared_tools.description:
Redact PII (emails, phone numbers, SSNs, credit cards, API keys) from text. Returns sanitized text with each entity replaced by a labeled placeholder, e.g. [EMAIL_REDACTED], [PHONE_REDACTED], [SSN_REDACTED], and the PII types found. Never returns the original text. Each call counts as one Request on your PromptGuard plan.
When to use: Before including user data in LLM prompts, when processing customer messages, or when building RAG pipelines that ingest documents containing personal information.

text.description: The text content to redact PII from

shared_tools.name: promptguard_status
shared_tools.title: PromptGuard status
shared_tools.description:
Show current PromptGuard configuration and status. Returns authentication state, plan or key type, and version.
When to use: To verify PromptGuard is properly configured, check which plan is active, or confirm the installed version.

cli_only_tools.name: promptguard_auth
cli_only_tools.title: Connect PromptGuard
cli_only_tools.description:
Check whether PromptGuard is authenticated, and if not, open the PromptGuard dashboard so the user can create an API key. This tool never takes the key itself: the user saves it outside the chat, by running `promptguard login` in a terminal or by setting PROMPTGUARD_API_KEY in this MCP server's configuration. Never ask the user to paste an API key into the conversation.
When to use: When any other promptguard tool reports that the user is not authenticated or not initialized, or when the user asks to log in to PromptGuard.
cli_only_tools.reason: Requires interactive browser access and local filesystem for credential storage

cli_only_tools.name: promptguard_logout
cli_only_tools.title: Log out of PromptGuard
cli_only_tools.description:
Log out of PromptGuard by removing the project-local configuration (.promptguard.json) and the globally stored API key (~/.promptguard/credentials.json).
When to use: When the user wants to switch PromptGuard accounts, clear credentials, or ensure a clean state by removing existing authentication.
cli_only_tools.reason: Requires local filesystem access to delete credentials

cli_only_tools.name: promptguard_scan_project
cli_only_tools.title: Find unprotected LLM calls
cli_only_tools.description:
Performs static analysis on a project directory to detect unprotected LLM SDK usage (OpenAI, Anthropic, Cohere, Gemini, Bedrock, etc.). Returns detected providers, file locations (line/column), and instance count.
When to use: During local development to find LLM calls that are not routed through PromptGuard, after generating new code that uses LLM SDKs, or when auditing an existing project for security coverage.

directory.description: Absolute path to the project directory to scan (defaults to current directory)

provider.description: Filter results to a specific provider (e.g. 'openai', 'anthropic')

cli_only_tools.reason: Requires local filesystem access and Tree-sitter AST parsing

backend_only_tools.name: promptguard_scan_code
backend_only_tools.title: Find LLM SDK calls in code
backend_only_tools.description:
Analyze code for LLM SDK usage patterns (OpenAI, Anthropic, Cohere, Google Gemini, Bedrock). Detects import statements and client instantiations via pattern matching.
When to use: After generating new code that uses LLM SDKs, when reviewing pull requests, or when auditing a codebase for security coverage gaps.

code.description: The code content to analyze for LLM SDK usage

backend_only_tools.reason: Operates on code strings (no filesystem). Backend handles this for hosted clients like ChatGPT.
